concern verb

be about, matter to

also as far as I’m concerned, it’s no concern of yours, apply to, relate to, as far as I am concerned, for all I care, it doesn’t matter to me, it has nothing to do with me

classical

Plaut. Trin. 1065: quid id ad mē attinet?
Traupman 294
Traupman 295

attinet (ad)

verb: third person of attineō, with ad and the accusative

it concerns, it has to do with

Quod ad mē attinet, as far as I am concerned (Cic. Q. fr. 2.1, Att. 5.17, Lewis & Short). Often shortened: istae quid ad mē?, what have these to do with me? (Plaut. Pers. 497).

Other words

  • pertinet (ad) — it concerns, it relates to

    verb: third person of pertineō, with ad and the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 36: illa rēs ad meum officium pertinet (Lewis & Short); Traupman 103: it doesn’t matter to me, nihil ad mē pertinet

  • rēfert (meā, tuā …) — it matters (to me, to you)

    impersonal verb, with meā, tuā or a genitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 497: et tuā rēfert; Traupman 294, 302; Traupman 295

    Interest is used the same way: meā interest, it matters to me (Traupman 302).

  • per mē (licet) — as far as I’m concerned, for all I care

    per with the accusative of the person: “as far as it depends on me”; usually with licet · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.29.93: per mē vel stertās licet (Lewis & Short), s.v. per; Traupman 98; Traupman 295; Traupman 313

    Lewis & Short s.v. per: “as far as concerns me, you”. With licet it gives leave: per mē licet, I have no objection.

Examples

  • quid id ad mē attinet?

    what has that to do with me?Plaut. Trin. 1065

  • Istae quid ad mē? — Immō ad tē attinent et tuā rēfert.

    What have these to do with me? — Oh, they concern you, and it matters to you.Plaut. Pers. 497

  • tantumne est ab rē tuā ōtī tibi, aliēna ut cūrēs eaque nihil quae ad tē attinent?

    have you so much time to spare from your own affairs that you look after other people’s, which don’t concern you?Ter. Heaut. 75–76 (Parry’s text)

  • nam tua rēs agitur, pariēs cum proximus ārdet

    for it is your concern when the wall next door is on fireHor. Ep. 1.18.84

  • Meā (tuā) minimē rēfert.

    It does not concern me (you) at all.Traupman 295

See also concern, question, business, interest.
